chunks: I say: If a thinker reflects upon his (peace be upon him) phrase, 'And whoever sees through it, it will bestow him sight,' he will find beneath it a wondrous meaning and a far-reaching purpose, whose ultimate goal cannot be reached and whose depth cannot be fathomed. Particularly when he associates with it his phrase, 'And whoever has his eye on it, it will blind him,' for he will find the difference between 'saw through it' and 'had his eye on it' clear, bright, wondrous, and shining! May the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him.

key_terms.أَبْصَرَ إِلَيْهَا: Had his eye on it (directed gaze towards it)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between seeing through something and looking at it in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Raḍī elucidates the subtle linguistic distinction in Imam Ali’s (AS) saying between 'seeing through' (biha) the world, which grants spiritual clarity, and 'looking at' it (ila), which causes spiritual blindness. This commentary highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the depth of perception, where true insight transcends superficial observation to reveal the divine reality within creation.
